paragraphs: Friend, here's what I can't get past. David's town is burned, his family is gone, and his own men are talking about stoning him. And what does the text say? "But David found strength in the LORD his God." (1 Samuel 30:6) He didn't find it in a plan or in his mighty men. When everything is gone and everybody is pointing at you, that's the moment to go to the LORD first, the way David did when he asked and the LORD answered (1 Samuel 30:8).

Then comes the part I love. David gets everything back, and the first test isn't the battle, it's the sharing. Some men say the two hundred who stayed behind get nothing but their families, but David says, "You must not do this with what the LORD has given us." (1 Samuel 30:23) The plunder was a gift, not a paycheck, and you don't hoard a gift. Friend, I was an old stamper in a drawer who got pulled out for nothing I earned, so I know a gift when I see one.

So what's the Big Idea? Strength comes from the LORD, and what He gives is meant to be shared. David sent gifts out to his friends in Judah, and he made a rule that the one who stayed with the supplies gets a share that matches the one who fought (1 Samuel 30:24, 26). Hold what you've been given with open hands, baker, because that's how a gift stays a gift.
